paper_title: Thinking Slow, Fast Scaling Inference Compute with Distilled Reasoners
caption: : Majority voting.
model_annotation: The plot illustrates majority voting accuracy as a function of the number of completions (k), showing four line series with different marker/color combinations. The x-axis is labeled “Number of completions (k)”, uses a logarithmic-style base-2 labeling with tick marks at 2^0, 2^1, 2^2, 2^3, 2^4, 2^5, 2^6, 2^7, and 2^8 (from 2^0 to 2^8). The y-axis is labeled “Majority voting accuracy”, appears linear, and spans roughly from about 0.24 up to about 0.62 with labeled ticks at 0.3, 0.4, 0.5, and 0.6. One upper series is a dark-blue solid line with circle markers, starting near 0.43 at 2^0–2^1, rising to about 0.49 at 2^2, about 0.57 at 2^4, and ending near 0.61–0.62 at 2^8. A second upper series is a green solid line with triangle markers, beginning near 0.43 at 2^0–2^1, increasing to about 0.50 at 2^2, about 0.58–0.59 around 2^5, and ending near 0.61–0.62 at 2^8. One lower series is a light-blue solid line with circle markers, starting near 0.24–0.25 at 2^0–2^1, increasing to about 0.30 at 2^2, about 0.39 at 2^4, and ending near 0.44 at 2^8. A second lower series is a light-green solid line with triangle markers, beginning around 0.25 at 2^0–2^1, rising to about 0.31 at 2^2, about 0.41 around 2^5, and ending around 0.44 at 2^8; all four series increase with k and then level off toward the right side of the plot.
